marks.gloss_en: דתנן: נזיר חופף ומפספס, אבל לא סורק (no SupportKind names דתנן)
the mishna: a nazir washes [his hair] and parts it, but does not comb it
סבר לה כי הא דתניא: scraping to beautify is forbidden
the baraita: a person scrapes dung-crusts and wound-scabs from his flesh because of his pain
ואינהו כמאן סברוה -- כי הא דתניא: a person washes his face, hands and feet every day for his Maker's sake
the baraita: a person washes his face, hands and feet every day for the sake of his Maker
if baraita A is R' Yehuda's, say the seifa: his face, hands and feet are permitted -- but that removes hair!
baraita A, seifa: but his face, hands and feet -- permitted
איבעית אימא בקטן -- a child
ואיבעית אימא באשה -- a woman
ואיבעית אימא בסריס -- a eunuch
לימא פליגא דשמואל -- Shmuel said a person does all his needs with bread, so ruining food does not forbid
אמרי: פת לא מאיסא, הני מאיסי -- bread does not become repulsive; these [split olives] do
Shmuel: a person does all his needs with bread
לא סבר לה מר להא דאמר רב ששת ברדא שרי?! -- doesn't the master hold Rav Sheshet's ruling?
בר מיניה דמר, דאפילו בחול נמי לא סבירא ליה (= p_mz_barda_asur_bechol)
Ameimar and Rav Ashi washed [with the berada brought before them]
the stam: rather, both baraitot are R' Yehuda's -- the permitting one (A) too
Rav Yehuda: afar levinta is permitted
Rav Yosef: berada is a third aloe, a third myrtle and a third violets
splitting olives on Shabbat is forbidden (asked of Rav Sheshet; his answer implies it)
תנן, וחכמים אומרים נוטל ומחזיר. היכי דמי? אי דלא נתקלקלה הגומא -- שפיר קאמרי רבנן; אלא לאו אף על פי שנתקלקלה הגומא -- the Sages permit returning even when the cavity collapsed, so not all agree
the Sages: he takes [the pot] and returns [it]

לא, לעולם דלא נתקלקלה, והכא בחוששין קמיפלגי -- the case is one where the cavity did not collapse; they disagree whether we are concerned lest it collapse (= p_choshshin_shema_nitkalkela / p_ein_choshshin_shema_nitkalkela)
one master holds: we are concerned lest the cavity collapse
R' Elazar ben Azarya: a basket -- he tilts it on its side and takes [the pot], lest he take [it and ...]
Rav Huna: this daffodil branch -- if he inserted it, pulled it out, and inserted it again, it is permitted
Shmuel: this knife between bricks -- if he inserted it, pulled it out, and inserted it again, it is permitted
Mar Zutra (or Rav Ashi): in a hedge of reeds it is fine
the mishna: one who buries turnips and radishes under a vine, if some of its leaves were exposed, need not be concerned for kilayim, sheviit or tithes, and they may be taken on Shabbat
